newsitem.title: CHINA: China's investment growth up 20 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: China's investment growth up 20 pct in 1996.

text.p: Investment growth in China is forecast to reach 20 percent for 1996, while production is lagging in a country burdened by inefficient state enterprises, the China Securities newspaper said on Wednesday.

Statistics from the State Planning Commission showed an increase in investment in areas such as steel, timber and cement. The rate of investment growth was expected to outpace production in these sectors by 4.0 percent in 1996 after inflation, the newspaper said.

The State Planning Commission said problems and losses in the state enterprise sector could not be solved by boosting investment alone, but production performance must be improved along with the ability to respond to the market, it said.

Total investment grew by 16.2 percent in the first quarter, 18.6 percent in the second quarter and 19.3 percent in the third quarter, higher than production growth in the same periods, it said. It did not give an overall increase for production.
It said investment in steel production increased by 5.2 percent in the first quarter, 4.6 percent in the second quarter and 6.9 percent in the third quarter, it said.
